title: Minimize the Maximum Difference of Pairs
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, select p pairs of indices such that the maximum difference between any pair is minimized, with no index repeated.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, select p pairs of indices such that the maximum difference between any pair is minimized, with no index repeated. The difference between a pair is the absolute value of the difference between the two elements. Return the smallest possible maximum difference among all pairs.
constraints: Choose exactly p disjoint index pairs; p may be zero.
A pair's difference is the absolute difference of its values.
Return the smallest achievable maximum difference across the chosen pairs.
reference_solution:
def minimum_maximum_pair_difference(nums,p):
    nums=sorted(nums)
    def possible(limit):
        count=index=0
        while index+1<len(nums):
            if nums[index+1]-nums[index]<=limit:count+=1;index+=2
            else:index+=1
        return count>=p
    low=0;high=nums[-1]-nums[0]
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if possible(middle):high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return low

hints: Sort values and binary-search a candidate maximum difference.
For a fixed limit, scan left to right and greedily pair adjacent values whenever possible.
After forming a pair, skip both elements; count whether at least p pairs are formed.
The closest available partner for the smallest remaining value is adjacent, so taking it cannot reduce future feasibility; the predicate is monotone in the limit.
